V2 used a disjoint 65,536-address window with 8,192 hash-selected controls (4,153 positive and 4,039 negative), then completed 1,920 calls with no gain beyond rank 17. This establishes the control-integrity correction, not score efficacy or a rank bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The address enumerator, control allocator, feature set, outcome definition, or exposure budget changes.

lessons.title: Score retrospective next moves with complete denominator accounting
lessons.when: Testing a proposed next-direction score against a sealed sequence of acquisitions on a known curve.
lessons.use: Freeze each candidate vocabulary independently of the acquired target and rank candidates only from the current prefix. Report vocabulary coverage separately; include absent targets in the event denominator and loss; exclude the admitted quotient span; use worst-rank tie handling; and aggregate by run when runs share a curve, metric, or point vocabulary. Compare to a fixed nonadaptive baseline rather than to a correlation built from the same metric.
lessons.avoid: Inserting a held-out target into its own vocabulary, deleting out-of-vocabulary events, treating tied final-stage candidates as unique top-one hits, calling 180 acquisitions independent trials, or promoting a same-metric correlation to a prospective predictor.
lessons.boundary: On the retained Curve302 trajectories, neither tested adaptive score beat static quotient norm in its bounded literal-vector vocabulary. Coverage was 49/180 and 70/180, so this rejects only those retrospective score/vocabulary pairs. The full input and output bundle is not shipped with this checkout, and no prospective predictor, propagation theorem, or rank bound follows.
lessons.reopen_when: A new prospective protocol freezes an outcome-independent candidate universe, a target-aligned endpoint, a complete immutable input bundle, tie rules, and a separately justified control population.

lessons.title: Bind pointed-search continuations to maps, finite state, and archived observations
lessons.when: Replacing a point-search backend or continuing a fixed roster of pointed-quartic charts from a certified Mordell--Weil subgroup.
lessons.use: Freeze the exact chart maps, reduced model, ordered roster, executable identity, limits, raw result fields, and an explicit infinity check before comparing backends. Replay maps, square hits, returned points, and finite independence without rediscovering them. Preload a declared prime bank once for a fixed basis, and rotate the entire prior observation state into an immutable archive before producing the next live state. Require every continuation to bind its parent-state key and each map index exactly once.
lessons.avoid: Comparing affine square sets while ignoring infinity, roster order, return codes, or duplicate records; treating a timeout as coverage of an unrecorded denominator prefix; mixing PARI output with a GMP transcript; dropping prior observations during state rotation; or presenting a point-cloud replay as exact rank or saturation.
lessons.boundary: On the retained rank-26 and rank-22 controls, map and state replays validate the completed fixed 301-box PARI rosters and their lower-bound clouds. The measured prime-preload improvement and backend timings apply to the declared controls only; finite no-gain boxes and complete clouds remain lower-bound evidence, not a speed theorem or rank upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The chart maps, model, basis, prime bank, backend executable, resource limits, or roster identity changes; each change needs a new calibration and state binding.

lessons.title: Deduplicate pointed-quartic roots by their subgroup extension
lessons.when: Interpreting multiple rational roots or tied candidates from a pointed quartic attached to a known Mordell--Weil subgroup S.
lessons.use: Handle the chart projectively at Q, -Q and O. Map both roots exactly and identify P with Q-P through the shared extension S + ZP. Compare candidates by their exact integral subgroup extension or quotient line before counting a gain. Keep the birational chart map, its degree-two parameter map and the degree-four covering map distinct.
lessons.avoid: Counting the two roots over one rational parameter as independent directions, calling the birational pointed chart a nontrivial 2-covering torsor, using a Kummer label as a finite-atlas cost invariant, or promoting an externally attested height measurement without its hashed payloads.
lessons.boundary: The Curve302 symbolic chart identities, public points and finite-reduction facts are checked locally. Its 17-test coordinate-cost report remains external attestation because the cited parent-data bundle, patch and measurement outputs are absent; it gives no cross-fibre speed or rank-prediction theorem.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete immutable measurement bundle supports an independently specified cross-fibre benchmark with fixed anchor banks and exact subgroup endpoints.

lessons.title: Separate rank-growth and saturation-only restart budgets
lessons.when: A checkpointed point search may update its certified subgroup before reaching a declared rank target.
lessons.use: Count a rank gain and a same-rank finite-index enlargement in separate, explicit counters. Classify the exact basis transition before charging either counter, and accept a certified target rank before deciding whether another restart is allowed. Preserve the old controller and its cap as a regression rather than silently changing its meaning.
lessons.avoid: Charging saturation-only changes against the budget reserved for rank growth, treating a basis update as a rank gain, or reading budget exhaustion as a saturation or rank upper bound.
lessons.boundary: The Curve385 v2 policy proves only correct controller accounting on a frozen adverse path. It has no new point-search outcome and does not justify launching its unrun alternate-stage plan.
lessons.reopen_when: A new search introduces another group-changing state, a different target-rank definition, or a changed checkpoint schema; its transition classes and limits must then be specified again.

lessons.title: Close a specialization only when its exact subgroup and rank interval meet
lessons.when: A point-search or section-specialization pipeline proposes a fixed high-rank elliptic curve.
lessons.use: Start from a pinned known subgroup, process each proposed point with exact group arithmetic and record each rank increase. Give the final ordered basis to an independent rank-bound routine. Publish exact rank only when its lower and upper endpoints agree; otherwise retain the exact lower bound and interval.
lessons.avoid: Promoting a Schur or height triage hit to a new direction, calling a wider rank interval exact, or treating a generic lower bound as an exact specialized rank.
lessons.boundary: At the Newfamily T=83/6 specialization, eleven inherited sections and exactly three processed extra points give rank14 before PARI returns [14,14]. This certifies that curve only; it does not certify the family, other triage hits, or a search heuristic.
lessons.reopen_when: A new specialization has an exact ordered subgroup and an independently checked upper-bound computation with a declared interval.

lessons.title: Measure new relation rank after targeting untouched factor-base directions
lessons.when: Collecting principal-ideal relations for a declared class-group or Selmer residual quotient.
lessons.use: State any factor-base generation hypothesis explicitly, retain the exact norm-coordinate transport including its fixed square factor, and admit a reduced-base row only after every outside coordinate cancels. Select untouched degree-one ideals by their exact root/HNF condition, reduce each index-prime lattice in the binary-cubic Hessian metric, and measure new matrix rank separately from smooth occurrences, successful target boxes, touched columns, and target-column projection rank.
lessons.avoid: Discarding outside coordinates, treating a smooth norm or a forced target factor as a new independent direction, confusing a finite residual matrix with a class-group computation, or promoting a GRH-dependent quotient bound to an unconditional rank bound.
lessons.boundary: For the fixed MW16 field, an interval-certified GRH base at 37638 retained 33 supported rows. A 512-target batch added 331 independent supported rows and reduced the residual dimension from 3210 to 2879. Exact rank, an unconditional upper bound, and a completion-time prediction remain UNKNOWN.
lessons.reopen_when: A new field, factor base, local condition, coordinate transport, or residual target changes; rebuild the exact row provenance and state the applicable generation hypothesis again.

lessons.title: Apply a shared exact norm budget before enumerating root-lattice components
lessons.when: Enumerating rootless lattice completions subject to a global projection-norm bound.
lessons.use: Charge every residual ADE label against one exact shared budget before forming component products. Use rational LDL shells, exact integrality and primitivity tests, saturated kernels, and integral-isometry deduplication. Cache repeated root and factorization data and checkpoint inside an anchor, while retaining every admitted representative and its class isometry.
lessons.avoid: Giving each component the full budget, treating partial zero counts as classification evidence, rejecting a new class because it differs from an expected known frame, or using minimum-vector statistics as an isometry test.
lessons.boundary: The determinant-1092 computation classifies the declared D5-anchored Weyl cover: 10,098 sixth-vector representatives yield 208 rootless embeddings and 19 integral-isometry classes. Its same-enumerator replay is a consistency check, not independent completeness verification or a general runtime speed theorem.
lessons.reopen_when: The auxiliary lattice, root condition, anchor cover, global norm constraint, or claimed equivalence relation changes; establish the new cover and retain its complete witness packet before reusing this pruning rule.

lessons.title: Compare the transferred 2-Kummer class before using a quadratic twist point
lessons.when: A quadratic multisection or anti-invariant point is proposed as a new elliptic 2-Kummer direction.
lessons.use: Derive the chord and trace maps symbolically, then identify the twist's monic Kummer coordinate in the cubic etale algebra. Prove the square relation to the rational trace class before evaluating a panel. Verify every specialized square witness with arithmetic independent of the constructor, and keep branch splitting separate from the class comparison.
lessons.avoid: Treating a quadratic point as rational on the original fibre, using r-theta instead of the monic twist coordinate d(r-theta), or inferring rational-span dependence, point absence, or a full Selmer conclusion from an inherited Kummer image.
lessons.boundary: For the stated determinant-1092 anti-trace construction, the transfer equals the inherited trace class on eight controls and Curve302. That blocks this mechanism as a first-unlock discriminator; it does not exclude split branches, other classes, higher descent, or rational points on either twist.
lessons.reopen_when: A new cover has a different trace relation, cubic algebra, twist normalization, or certified non-inherited image; rerun the exact symbolic comparison for that construction.

lessons.title: Keep a rational norm quadric separate from its integral seed lattices
lessons.when: Two seed-relative norm equations appear to define different torsors or candidate arithmetic directions.
lessons.use: First give an explicit rational quadric, inverse parametrization and equation-only comparison. Then retain the distinct integral transport matrices, chart exceptions and basis order, and verify both rational and integral identities independently. Treat a rational quadric point as a starting coordinate fact only.
lessons.avoid: Discarding integral data after finding a rational parametrization, calling a trivial norm torsor an elliptic cover or rational point, or using a nine-control rationality result as a seed discriminator.
lessons.boundary: For the two determinant-1092 seed equations, one rational quadric and the same rational point occur on Curve302 and eight controls, while the integral lattices remain distinct and seed-derived. This neither settles the integral gate nor creates a new-parameter seed.
lessons.reopen_when: The cubic algebra, norm equations, integral basis, admissibility condition, or sought arithmetic conclusion changes; rederive both the rational and integral transports.

lessons.title: Compare score strata only on matched finite cohorts and full search cost
lessons.when: Choosing how to allocate a fixed point-search budget across retained score bands.
lessons.use: Freeze equally sized matched arms, preserve the matching calipers and selection inputs, complete every allocated box, and charge map construction and point-worker time consistently. Report certified directions, verification cost, censoring, family holdouts, and concentration of gains separately from the allocation decision.
lessons.avoid: Using a later high-rank point to refill an arm, comparing unequal or incompletely covered bands, calling discovery worker time elapsed wall time, or promoting a selected-sample yield advantage to a rank-density or rank-tail theorem.
lessons.boundary: In the retained 60-curve MW16 sample, the extreme-top arm found 10 directions, moderate 1, and lower 0, but nine top-band directions came from one curve. The finite matched comparison favours that arm for this pool only; it neither warrants an automatic sweep nor predicts a new population.
lessons.reopen_when: A new population, score definition, matching relation, worker policy, or point-proof cost changes; freeze and complete a fresh comparison rather than extending these arms.

lessons.title: Test split residual divisors directly when recovering a missing generic section
lessons.when: A frozen lower-rank generic core is used to seek one missing Mordell--Weil direction without exposing that section.
lessons.use: Freeze omissions, masks, centre order, degree bounds, resource limits and exact height-Gram admission before RR work. Construct residual divisors from retained sections, test their quadratic splitting over Q(t), and certify every recovered section against the full height Gram. Retain censored suffixes and complete per-arm evidence.
lessons.avoid: Calling sampled parity representatives coset minima, inferring a section from an abstract lattice class, refilling failed arms, or reading bounded misses as geometric inaccessibility or a general MW16-to-MW17 theorem.
lessons.boundary: Nine of seventeen determinant-1092 leave-one-out cores recovered the known seventeenth direction under one frozen policy. This is a positive calibration only; it creates no new surface, generic rank, selector validation, or exceptional-point result.
lessons.reopen_when: The parent, retained core, divisor family, degree policy, or quotient certificate changes; freeze a new protocol and retain every arm before comparison.

lessons.title: Separate fibration-level calibration from presentation-specific bounded boxes
lessons.when: Several coordinate presentations describe one generic MW lattice but change the actual specialized point-search box.
lessons.use: First certify base/Weierstrass equivalence and the shared specialized subgroup, then report target-level recovery separately from each frozen coordinate box. Keep blind controls, ordering inputs, chart masks, height bound and resource cap fixed. Use heuristic scores only to order candidates; require an exact bounded recovery before a residual-Selmer or other expensive gate. A replacement backend gets a new terminal receipt even when it reconstructs the same target set.
lessons.avoid: Counting coordinate labels as independent fibrations, merging point counts from different bounded boxes, treating an all-timeout pass as completed coverage, or promoting a bounded null result, control recovery, or selected-chart timing to a rank bound or population success rate.
lessons.boundary: The nine ICARM presentations reduce to five fibration classes but remain nested search charts. Their fixed blind calibration recovered 54 of 55 demonstrated directions; a later target-free direct backend completed 856 declared boxes with no gain. Neither result validates an unbounded search, a selector, or a rank upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The base/section transports, subgroup, chart maps, height box, ordering rule, backend, or expensive follow-on gate changes; re-establish equivalence and retain a separate receipt before comparing outcomes.

lessons.title: Certify the known Kummer image before starting relative descent
lessons.when: A known independent point basis will be removed from a 2-Selmer computation or relative-cover construction.
lessons.use: Pin the model, points and 2-division cubic; prove trivial rational 2-torsion; and certify the displayed basis rank in exact products of E(F_p)/2E(F_p). A bounded saturation routine may supply a shorter candidate basis, but admit it only after exact point membership and an independent full-rank finite-quotient certificate. Then subtract this certified Kummer dimension from a complete Selmer dimension before constructing residual covers.
lessons.avoid: Treating a mod-3-selected basis as full mod-2 input, promoting bounded ellsaturation to global saturation, interpreting a PARI output as a Selmer bound, or searching covers before removing the certified known subgroup.
lessons.boundary: For the four fixed near misses, the exact inputs have Kummer dimensions 20, 20, 19 and 19. They are descent inputs only: no complete Selmer group, residual cover, rank upper bound, or new rational point follows.
lessons.reopen_when: The curve, point basis, rational 2-torsion condition, finite-quotient certificate, or intended descent changes; rebuild and certify the Kummer image before reusing the relative quotient.

lessons.title: Replay a public baseline from retained arithmetic inputs, not its webpage
lessons.when: A published equation, family, or point list supplies a fixed elliptic-curve calibration or lower-bound replay.
lessons.use: Retain the exact formulas or model, every displayed coordinate, a compact certificate, and hashes binding the checker to those inputs. Make the replay read only repository files; keep citation URLs and retrieval dates as provenance. State separately which current-record, attribution, conditional-upper-bound, or unpublished-construction assertions the local packet cannot establish.
lessons.avoid: Downloading a replacement input during replay, treating a URL and old hash as sufficient evidence, silently updating a public point list, or promoting a fixed finite-reduction lower bound to an exact rank or current-record claim.
lessons.boundary: The retained Kihara formulas at t=2 and the retained 29-point public record each support their exact stated lower bound without upstream access. They do not certify current external rankings, conditional upper bounds, a further point, or a different specialization.
lessons.reopen_when: The formula/model/coordinate packet, certificate criterion, or intended claim changes; preserve a new complete projection and compare it to the old packet before replaying.

lessons.title: Bound a six-root parent search in primitive coordinates
lessons.when: A known elliptic curve is absent from a bounded six-root parent census.
lessons.use: Record the labelled rational roots, affine scale and translation, parameter scale, and the resulting primitive integral root tuple. Set the search bound on that primitive diameter, then verify the exact model change and transported generic section.
lessons.avoid: Treating a miss in a normalized coordinate box as absence of a parent family, or using a matching j-invariant without an exact Weierstrass change.
lessons.boundary: For ICARM curve 245, the earlier diameter-300 census could not see the recovered parent because its primitive integral diameter is 731. This recognition result recovers a parent; it does not transfer the specialized rank to nearby fibres.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed family has a different equivalence relation, root labelling, or primitive-bound convention.

lessons.title: Keep a rebuilt replay in a named successor lineage
lessons.when: A historical checker cannot run because its immutable source artifact or toolchain is unavailable, but a compatible exact source chain can be rebuilt.
lessons.use: Keep the historical program and its expected digest unchanged. Write a separate successor wrapper that asserts replacement input digests and writes a distinct schema and output path. If a new independent global proof becomes available, register it separately rather than retagging the historical record.
lessons.avoid: Retagging a rebuilt output as the historical artifact, relaxing a frozen input assertion, overwriting the old output path, or treating a bounded successor sieve as the missing global proof.
lessons.boundary: The H3 source successor and bounded quotient sieve remain distinct current replay records. The later Sage quadratic-Chabauty certificate proves the rational base independently; it does not recreate the historic Magma output.
lessons.reopen_when: The original inputs and runtime become available for a byte-identical historical replay, or another frozen certificate needs a successor lineage.

lessons.title: Close an even genus-two curve with two rank-one elliptic quotients
lessons.when: An even sextic y^2=a6*x^6+a4*x^4+a2*x^2+a0 has two explicit elliptic quotients with unconditional rank one and trivial torsion, and a global rational-point proof is required.
lessons.use: Pin a bielliptic quadratic-Chabauty implementation, use two good ordinary primes with a compatible finite height-value ordering, normalize quotient coordinates at a rational base point, close p-adic roots under the curve automorphisms, CRT their coordinates modulo p^N, then eliminate the remaining classes by exact good-reduction images.
lessons.avoid: Treating one p-adic pass, a bounded multiple search, or a finite reduction sieve by itself as completeness; and claiming the direct quotient-coordinate lattice is a saturated Jacobian basis when only its necessary quotient condition is used.
lessons.boundary: The method certifies only the displayed curve and the pinned implementation, primes, precision and finite sieve. It requires exact quotient rank and torsion certificates and does not construct a downstream surface or fibration equation. An offline replay must supply the one SHA-checked upstream source through --upstream-source; a cache miss otherwise downloads only the pinned revision.
lessons.reopen_when: The model, quotient maps, rank certificates, implementation hash, p-adic precision or candidate-eliminating prime set changes.

lessons.title: Transfer a labeled finite-reduction certificate to generic rank
lessons.when: Explicit sections of an elliptic family are available and one smooth rational specialization may establish a generic rank lower bound.
lessons.use: Verify the section identities over the function field, preserve their labels through one good specialization, select only the needed points, and stack exact E(F_p)/lE(F_p) columns until they have full rank. Add a good-reduction exclusion of rational l-torsion, then invoke specialization to transfer that selected independent subgroup to the generic fibre.
lessons.avoid: Sorting or changing branches separately at each reduction, treating all displayed sections as independent, or replacing the torsion check with a bounded relation search.
lessons.boundary: This proves only the lower bound supplied by the selected labeled sections. It gives neither generic rank equality, saturation, independence of unused companions, nor an exact conductor statement.
lessons.reopen_when: The family formulas, labeled section roster, specialization, reduction prime set, or torsion exclusion changes.

lessons.title: Keep unresolved quotient transports as literal unknowns
lessons.when: A finite population of specialized elliptic fibres has a mixture of exact displayed-subgroup transports and uncompiled chart-specific quotient data.
lessons.use: Bind the population and each marked-U chart to a profile artifact. Retain only exact transports as exact, leave every other dimension null, and select a new tranche solely by a declared arithmetic criterion such as the maximum certified specialized rank lower bound. For each selected row, require a saturated generic transport, exact specialization and group-law relations, displayed-subgroup independence, and a Smith-form quotient proof.
lessons.avoid: Treating a null as a zero quotient, copying a transport across PGL2 or lattice-equivalent markings, reopening a completed tranche, or using public hit counts as a success-rate denominator or priority score.
lessons.boundary: A displayed-subgroup quotient is not the quotient of the full Mordell--Weil group and gives no rank upper bound. The selected initial tranche is a reproducible work priority, not evidence that it has positive quotient rank or that deferred rows are unpromising.
lessons.reopen_when: The marked-U transport, certified rank lower bounds, population membership, or exact quotient data changes.

lessons.title: Require quotient-invariant local data before using Kummer information as a selector
lessons.when: Comparing fixed high-rank specializations for a shared local Kummer signature that might justify congruence filtering or a parameter search.
lessons.use: Present the displayed directions as V/R before choosing any complement. Compare only local Kummer and component data that descend through R; for each componentwise Hilbert form B, check R*B=0 before treating it as a quotient tensor. If the retained quotient-invariant signatures disagree, preserve the exact obstruction primes and terminate that selector route.
lessons.avoid: Building a graph from RREF nonpivot coordinates, treating the identically trivial corestricted local Tate form as a coupling signal, turning a fixed-pair mismatch into a global nonexistence theorem, or launching a parameter search merely because a local diagnostic was computed.
lessons.boundary: The gate concerns the stated quotient presentation and selected fibres. It proves neither a full Mordell--Weil quotient nor a rank upper bound, and it leaves mechanisms based on different invariant data open.
lessons.reopen_when: A different quotient-compatible invariant, a changed visible relation space, or an independently justified family-wide mathematical gate is available.

lessons.title: Use certified local height bounds to compare complementary models of the same pointed chart
lessons.when: Comparing equivalent pointed quartic models for a fixed elliptic equation and anchor, before choosing search boxes.
lessons.use: Compose the exact x(2P-Q) map with each parameter matrix. Bound its real norm on the soluble compact projective charts, and refine the uniform Bezout cancellation divisor using complete finite residue trees with proved nonsquare exclusions. Keep unprocessed primes and branches conservatively. For multiple minimal models, retain joint local cells and take max over cells of min over complete models. Charge construction, bounds, failed attempts, point calls and verification in the next-direction benchmark.
lessons.avoid: Choosing a model by coefficient size alone, confusing a smaller sufficient height bound with containment of every old search box, summing model-wise minima independently across primes, or calling a rational-address work proxy a CPU or rank-gain prediction.
lessons.boundary: One actual Curve302 chart supplies independently replayed bounds and three certified minimal models. The base-plus7-neighbour pair has approximately1.48033 improvement in sufficient per-box height and0.91266 address-work ratio, but no new point search or speed advantage. The finite bounds need not be optimal. The old factor-free model is a comparator, not one of the three minimal models.
lessons.reopen_when: A frozen next-direction comparison pays for its new preparation and then transfers to independently sourced withheld directions on other curves.

lessons.title: Separate cold support, uniform coverage and actual target accessibility
lessons.when: Benchmarking a certified height-based model selector at the supplied equation, subgroup and anchor interface.
lessons.use: Freeze model vocabulary and exact pair-height allocation before search; charge required support discovery and verification. After all endpoints are sealed, transport each literal winning point into every model and verify its parameter height and exact slack decomposition log(C/g)/4 plus log(S/L)/4. Keep diagnostics separate from arm costs and target-informed selection.
lessons.avoid: Treating cached discriminant factors as free cold preparation, hiding a preparation timeout as a point-search miss, assuming the smallest uniform bound gives the smallest coordinate for each point, or using a distinct-prime product partition for two neighbours at one prime.
lessons.boundary: On three Curve302 controls the baseline recovers the next direction, while all six bounded arms hit a30-second support limit and make no point calls. Twelve individual-model coordinates replay; the best uniform bound selects a smallest actual coordinate only in the first row. Finite cancellation dominates the slack. This is a three-target conditional diagnostic, not a general performance or probability statement. The same-prime pair is UNKNOWN only for the frozen formula.
lessons.reopen_when: A specifically revised, bounded preparation or model-selection policy addresses the measured bottleneck and receives a new complete-cost comparison; no automatic rerun or budget enlargement.

lessons.title: Optimize complete coverage with unequal box heights and explicit model costs
lessons.when: A certified complete joint-state table for equivalent models of one marked chart is already available.
lessons.use: At a declared elliptic-height range X, compute exact ceil((X D_i(s))^(1/4)) thresholds. Minimize a supplied monotone cost over boxes meeting at least one model threshold for every joint state. Charge activation separately from all-bank preparation, including discarded models. Check the finite optimum by independent state assignments; keep the statewise choice coupled across all places.
lessons.avoid: Treating minimization of a shared coverage constant as the whole cost problem, dropping discarded-model preparation, calling an equal H-squared price a CPU calibration, or using uniform coverage as a probability model for the first independent point.
lessons.boundary: The earlier equal-box selector already charged model count through |T|^2 D_T. On its unchanged three-model/four-state first chart, unequal heights yield an exact 0.573942907264 address-proxy ratio to the best single, or 0.599197887808 with at most two models. This does not resolve cold support timeouts or the observed targetwise finite-cancellation slack. No search was run or selector deployed into the sealed benchmark.
lessons.reopen_when: A bounded preparation and independently calibrated pricing policy is frozen for a new complete-cost comparison. Transfer needs independently sourced cross-curve targets; proxy optimization alone does not authorize a campaign.

lessons.title: Verify integral orders and the backend input contract before global Selmer arithmetic

The supplied-basis example X^2-20 returns[] for the nonmaximal order of discriminant80.
lessons.boundary: Cases09 and08 have verified model and field maps and integral orders, but no certified maximal order or global Selmer dimension. lessons.title: Count normalization delta with infinity and keep the high-rank parent fixed
lessons.when: Forcing two polynomial trace-zero bisections of arithmetic genus5 to share a quadratic cover of genus0 or1.
lessons.use: Write F=x^3+A*x+B and its jet conditions. At a root of multiplicity m use delta=floor(m/2), and include the missing multiplicity at infinity in the degree12 binary form. Impose one literal D in both identities. Extract repeated factors D=e^2*d before deciding the genus: residual degree2 gives a possible genus0 boundary. Reuse the height8 independence criterion when the branch avoids the parent discriminant. For a fixed constant-abscissa line, the degree33 critical-point polynomial and critical-value norm can certify its entire singularity locus by exact interpolation and a good-prime squarefreeness witness. For the complete coefficient chart, factor the difference identity with g=gcd(D,h), u=gcd(h/g,r1-r2) and v=(h/g)/u after monic normalization. Keep all15 degree allocations and nine good coordinate patches; the squarefree height cross term is4-k-2*j. On Q80 use unramified Kummer descent to eliminate the complete k=4 genus-one case before any elimination. For genus0 pass to the full f(x_i)=q*s_i^2 chart with deg s_i<=5; repeated common-quartic models unnecessarily force a shared linear node factor. Keep all12 degree allocations. In the Q80 k2,j1 case use inherited unramified descent and the complete arithmetic-genus1 singular exclusion before coefficient elimination. After same-branch genus0 descent, the cross-height+/-2 cases have a smooth rational half-image. Reuse the complete branch atlas and exclude parent2-torsion over its residue fields with simple degree-one prime witnesses. Monic cubic integrality handles unbounded coordinates; specialization at ramification then forces anti-invariant height at least12. Before searching for a high-rank fibration on a new control surface, a complete good-prime surface count gives the cheap necessary bound rho_Q <= floor((22*p+#X(Fp)-1-p^2)/(2*p)). Subtract2 for any rational Jacobian fibration. Retain infinity and count a nodal cubic itself, not its normalization. Distinguish a cubic root from complete splitting and a square discriminant from a root. For a local full-splitting witness retain three distinct Hensel balls satisfying v(f)>2*v(f_prime) and pairwise disjoint error radii. Exact rational replay handles bad primes and weighted infinity without trusting approximate p-adic roots. Before coefficient elimination, pair the ramified norm-square class with inherited unramified alpha_T=X_T-theta by Weil reciprocity. Its odd divisor Z must satisfy Norm_Z(alpha_T) square for every T. For a single complementary fibre divisor this reduces to X_T(b)-e square. A complete good-prime root roster with one nonvanishing nonsquare character per point excludes that whole stratum. Recheck literal rational section identities and all infinity reductions; independence of the witness sections is unnecessary. For a degree2 branch divisor evaluate both selected-root norm-character vectors over the complete quadratic residue field. Use3*e^2+A when an inherited section meets the selected2-torsion root, and squareclass1 at a pole. Include roots with multiplicity at nodal quadratic residues. Distinguish rational branch pairs, unramified quadratic fields with rational or quadratic base residue, and ramified quadratic fields before deducing a coefficient congruence. After a genus0 branch collision is forced at a smooth fibre, first prove coefficient integrality using the flat divisor limit of the rational bisection and properness of genus0 stable maps. Treat the literal scalar valuation and constant nonsquare twist before enumerating reduced points. Recompute the finite basis Gram and use character rank and index-square divisibility to prove full saturation. Enumerate the complete norm4 lattice with exact rational LDL bounds, identify every polynomial point and test the full coefficient Jacobian, including homogeneous infinity. A simple ordinate zero has only its inherited split Hensel lift. Repeated contacts can support a nonsplit lift only if both required root labels survive at the same fibre. For genus1 k2, apply degree2 reciprocity to the unused root of P1-P2; this is only one norm condition. Use complete individual character codes and their pairwise XORs to classify both agreement and disagreement divisors. For a genus1 denominator limit, count positive-genus components and retain the actual zero-section multiplicity. A fourth-power smooth-fibre limit would require four unramified elliptic preimages and four separate nonconstant O tails, exceeding its O degree2. Keep the all-nodal case. With integral coefficients, compare complete reduced norm4 contact pairs and augment the full shared-quartic Jacobian by the first error from the literal coefficients modulo p^2. Use exact residue interpolation to cut a remaining polynomial search to p or p^3 tuples, including arbitrary scalar classes, and independently reconstruct square roots in the opposite coefficient direction. For a surviving nodal boundary, the anisotropic quadratic and quartic invariant give necessary local rational-point and j-valuation conditions. At an I1 denominator boundary, split off the analytic simple cubic root rho and prepare x-rho and r in the residue disc. Count their zeros with multiplicity before choosing a valuation scale. A double zero of x-rho uses one r zero; differentiating the remaining U^2-V contact determines the scale and its second derivative excludes higher contacts. Compare the abscissa difference quotient with the two analytic node-root labels on the common smaller branch disc. If each section must switch labels, partial branch agreement is impossible. Verify the implicit derivative of rho from the actual cubic coefficients, not from a polynomial representing only its residue value. Retain an exact local section control and distinguish split, unramified and ramified branch fields. A rational agreement branch at a good residue can force genus1 coefficient integrality. With one smooth and three nodal residues, a primitive simple abscissa zero produces three distinct simple zeros against the three analytic cubic-root functions, contradicting a single branch zero. Once integral, the agreement residue cannot collide with disagreement. Odd total multiplicity at a repeated cubic residue leaves a nonzero rational unused-root character. For squarefree degree3 disagreement, impose both its zero unused-root norm and its selected-root norm matching the rational agreement code. Reuse rational/quadratic tables and enumerate every nonrational cubic base orbit. A Frobenius splitting test avoids scanning all possible cubic roots; keep nodal root multiplicity and regularized zeros/poles. Replay using different extension-field and polynomial arithmetic, direct Q-power versus repeated p-Frobenius, and indexed joins instead of all composite tuples. For k0 impose both selected-root norms, hence zero for all three root divisors. Join complete signatures for every degree partition; exclude proper-subfield elements from a genuine degree4 census. A tower with i^2=-1,j^2=1+i permits fast exact Cardano tests, with monomial/Tonelli-Shanks replay and ten source-bound checkpoints. Stop each fibre only after an actual failing character. For square reductions enumerate every binary quadratic divisor of both ordinates, retaining multiplicity and infinity, and test the divided first-lift error rather than Jacobian rank alone. At a nodal disc write f=(x-rho)*(U^2-V), with V having a simple zero. If both branch selections are simple and x is bounded analytic with negative Gauss valuation and primitive order at least2, preparation makes U^2-V an analytic square up to an unramified constant extension. The product (U+Z)*(U-Z)=V then violates zero counts. Apply the height formula to the sum and difference, descend their O-intersection divisors away from ramification, and compare the pole degree with the residual degree of the nodal disc. A degree0 or1 pole divisor cannot reach an irreducible quadratic disc; a degree2 pole divisor can. In the mixed nodal case first solve the simple cubic root modulo q0 squared and enumerate its131 remaining quartic coefficients, including every constant twist. A unique ordinary seed can make the13-by14 coefficient Jacobian a formal one-parameter branch. Use a unit discriminant derivative and integral branch-centre coefficients to compare its smoothing valuation with the negative-section separation law; this can force, rather than assume, a denominator valuation. Evaluate the exact inherited word at the lifted nodal base value using the multiplicative or projective nodal group law, and compare the resulting necessary leading scalar with its required constant residue field. For a negative meromorphic abscissa with one double pole in a nodal disc and primitive numerator order4, prepare a square root Z of U squared-V after clearing the fourth-order pole. Choose the leading sign and count zeros minus poles of U+Z, not just its zeros. Degree2 forces U+Z=p^(-2L)*h*(t-xi) squared with h integral unit and xi different from the node. Its contacts with the analytic unit root of F squared-3rho F+V are two simple branch points at separation L. Count those forced contacts before considering any closer roots on the small analytic branch. Formal-group addition of original points with aligned leading terms preserves L and supplies a contradiction when their branch separation is greater.
lessons.avoid: Treating a zero discriminant or a bounded coefficient miss as a four-node or full-family theorem; rejecting every repeated quartic as unusable; losing constant squareclasses or infinity; or solving for new A,B and claiming to have kept an inherited MW17 parent. Equal branch-root choices can force halving only after proving the everywhere-unramified class is inherited. An inherited mod2 class alone does not make the underlying point inherited. A high-genus splitting curve does not exclude its low-degree closed points. Initial bad-prime reductions without simple roots can acquire local points after base/x coordinate changes. A degree-one residue witness needs an integral parent and an etale branch reduction; leading-coefficient loss or a repeated branch root is a deferral. Testing the branch field does not bound the entire twist rank or the splitting curve outside that atlas. Do not infer a geometric Picard bound from rational Frobenius-p classes, promote an upper bound to an exact rank, omit the infinity fibre, or assume that a new fibration can evade a bound on the entire rational Neron-Severi group. Every retained parent now has a full local split fibre at each of the original fourteen primes2 through43. Do not rerun this panel to seek an empty local splitting curve, infer global divisors from local points or CRT compatibility, or infer local solubility of the full coefficient system from its necessary splitting condition. Full cubic splitting alone misses these reciprocity constraints. Do not turn a single-point contradiction into an exclusion of one closed point of degree2/3/4: the norm characters can cancel across its conjugates. In the single-point shortcut, a zero ordinate or pole requires another witness; the coupled calculation instead uses regularized squareclasses. A singular residue fibre cannot be silently omitted. Do not reject a quadratic branch divisor merely because its reduction is nonreduced, or confuse that branch-map degeneration with bad reduction of its abstract conic. Refining the same local characters cannot exclude discs where distinct close branch pairs already satisfy all norms. A degeneration argument must identify the actual flat image cycle, not merely its numerical divisor class. Do not assume integral coefficients from a finite-field miss, discard odd or nonsquare scalar classes, trust a partial section roster as the full reduced MW group, or declare a residue excluded just because a single Jacobian is singular. Do not import the genus0 two-character condition into genus1 k2: only the unused root is constrained on its degree2 disagreement divisor. A genus1 stable-map limit can contain one elliptic component, so the genus0 integrality proof alone does not apply. A full-rank Jacobian does not exclude a lift without its inconsistent error vector. A local denominator boundary is not a positive coefficient solution or a complete stratum exclusion. Do not use a bounded denominator sweep as the nodal orientation theorem, assume the residual simple-root representative has the correct derivative, or assume ordinary contacts before checking the dominant second-derivative term. Weierstrass preparation requires the primitive local series and its exact reduction order. Even contact valuation alone does not force splitting over Q_p. Finite derivative and toy-control replay does not formally verify the analytic proof. Do not infer a cubic disagreement solution from its unused-root norm alone: the other code must be one of the rational agreement characters. Ramified degree3 fields contribute the total local degree to the reduced norm. A squarefree base reduction can still lie over a nodal parent fibre and must be retained. A k0 quartic reducing to q0 squared need not factor as two quadratic fields over Q_p; the earlier k2 orientation proof requires that field hypothesis. Do not assume every surviving contact quadratic is irreducible: the30 actual k0 pairs include split quadratics. Do not include F_p-squared base elements in the genuine degree4 norm census; the extra even extension trivializes their characters. An empty finite norm census does not exclude nonreduced nodal reductions or prove both abscissas negative. Do not extend the pole-free zero-count contradiction across a meromorphic pole, confuse poles of the sum/difference with branch factors, assume the two pole divisors are disjoint, or infer that the branch quartic splits over the field of those poles. Reduction at the coefficient Gauss valuation must be justified on the good generic fibre. Checked finite premises and a height table do not independently or formally verify a new analytic proof. A high-precision p-adic contact is not exact evidence without a unit/error bound or independent modular replay. Evaluate at the actual discriminant lift, not just a residue representative. Do not infer a rational global family from a formal parameter, discard the nonsquare unit twist without testing it, or reuse the mixed-case seed/denominator bound when both original points reduce to O. Do not stop after showing both given branches must lie on the small analytic root: the unit-root equation still has two forced simple contacts and they must consume the same branch divisor. Do not infer the simple contact from residue counting alone; the derivative of F has negative valuation while the analytic unit-root derivative is integral. Keep the xi=alpha possibility in the divisor-degree check. The new lemma requires exactly one double pole in the disc; higher pole budgets are outside it.

lessons.title: Predict realized cancellation through q-conditioned residue states and test complete CPU cost

Compute residue masses and cancellation expectations using only N,D,q; compare uniform soluble and differential-weighted p^(v(q)/2) reference measures. lessons.title: Use rational tangent points for the first singular elliptic-bisection layer
lessons.when: Seeking genus-one quadratic covers beyond smooth bisection pencils on a24-I1 elliptic K3.
lessons.use: For arithmetic-genus2 images, normalize trace modulo twice the inherited MW group and pass to the quotient by T-P. Its F1 branch curve has genus9. A genuine genus-one normalization comes from a rational tangent point with exactly one contact of order2 or3; test its tangent line, integral pullback, residual quartic and rational base. For any smooth-branch cover, use h(anti-trace)=4*(p_a+3) to certify independence from a nonsquare genus ratio once the literal cover is identical. For an inherited rational contact in this layer, require h(T-2R)>=14 before interpolation. Recover a retained height-four word over Q by seven exact fibre evaluations, verify its polynomial equation, and use the intersection bound to attach it to the word; finite-field coordinates alone are insufficient. For arithmetic genus4, use a degree-three contact divisor on the F1 halving curve. Construct its Hermite lift modulo f^2 and test the three-by-two high-coefficient matrix before solving the full six jets. Rank1, homogeneous coprimality, actual incidence and a squarefree residual quartic are separate required checks. Infinite arithmetic supply would force a degree-three elliptic quotient; a contact-parameter elliptic curve is not the covering base. At equality in Castelnuovo-Severi, compare the same intrinsic adjoint line bundle on the forced smooth product model and on the ruled quotient. On F1, restriction of |2C0+F| retains C0.R as a fixed divisor; on a (3,4) curve in P1 times an elliptic curve, three explicit chart-glued adjoint sections have no common zero. Apply this obstruction before a cubic elliptic-map or Jacobian campaign.
lessons.avoid: Searching an unbounded two-parameter net as if rational one-node members formed a free rational family, mistaking rational singular points of the plane or dual curve for rational points of the normalization, or treating finiteness as an effective enumeration.
lessons.boundary: Finiteness is for arithmetic genus2 and normalization genus1 modulo inherited translations over a fixed number field. It does not exclude all such members or higher arithmetic genus. The height identity requires smooth parent branch fibres. A square height ratio proves neither dependence nor independence. Symbolic premises are checked but the geometric and Faltings arguments are written. For Q80 trace P3, the complete retained height-four shell at distance h(P3-2R)=14 has 230 oriented sections and no rational contact, including poles and infinity. Exact degree-five/degree-thirteen factors have modular no-root witnesses. This is a bounded experiment, not an all-height or all-trace exclusion. The cubic-contact constructor supplies no actual halving point. Although the genus9 Castelnuovo-Severi bound reaches equality for a degree-three elliptic quotient, its smooth product model makes |K_R-2L| basepoint-free, contradicting the fixed length-two divisor on F1. That quotient is now geometrically excluded and the arithmetic-genus4 layer is finite modulo translations. Exceptional contacts remain unenumerated; larger-degree elliptic maps and higher image genera are outside the result.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual eligible rational tangent point yields a literal quartic matching another independent bisection cover, with an infinite rational covering base, or a new construction addresses higher arithmetic-genus images.

Combine I=N+l-2 with the flow valuation bound N<=m*l/2 and then charge the local Q pole degree globally.

The unique degree8/polar33 gcd chain forces w order2 and contradicts critical flow27 versus24. lessons.title: Integrate ambient source lengths before normalizing a special image fibre

lessons.title: Apply fixed-sheet inertia and normal-closure obstructions before affine completion
lessons.when: A finite transitive action or a branched cover is proposed as generic monodromy of a polynomial Keller self-map of affine space in characteristic zero.

For natural PSL2(11), replace derangement finite inertia and audit F11 as a rational cover input. Track geometric and arithmetic groups separately using the exact discriminant constant.

lessons.title: Exclude low-degree constant Jacobian pairings before sparse algebra
lessons.when: A normalized low-degree three-variable Keller collision candidate is considered.
lessons.use: Reject completed supports with a nonlinear univariate coordinate or a nonconstant normal derivative on a coordinate hyperplane. In degree at most ten, a constant nonzero v^T*JF*w is excluded by a triangular source reduction to a plane map of degree at most D^2<=100 and Moh. For normalized maps search the finite bilinear direction incidence. The complete size-eight cover has 17435 univariate, 46 elementary-shear, and one hyperplane-normal-factor orbit.

lessons.boundary: The univariate and hyperplane-normal-factor gates are arbitrary-degree necessities. The pairing gate imports Moh's degree-100 plane theorem. The special-form minimum four is for degree-at-most-ten counterexamples admitting a constant nonzero pairing, with a degree-seven stabilized witness; it is not an unrestricted dimension minimum.
lessons.reopen_when: The completed candidate passes all three gates, exceeds degree ten for the pairing reduction, or supplies a new plane theorem.

lessons.title: Use the complete affine-W generating-function classification before dense cubic search
lessons.when: A ternary Gaussian polynomial is W*h(Z)+v(Z)*T^2+u(Z)*T+r(Z), including either h(0) chart.
lessons.use: Apply GL1, then integrate the scalar Gaussian quadratic. On h(0)!=0 rational-exponential rigidity forces (h-Z*hprime)^2*(h-2Z*v)=h^3 and 2*(h-2Z*v)*r+Z*u^2=0; the root argument forces h constant or linear. On h(0)=0 evaluate the fixed point at zero and retain the separate one-sided branch. In total degree D>=2, use the sufficient 5D-3 pure-moment gate; the quartic failure locus is exactly the linear repair k0+k1*Z.

lessons.title: Use a Hamiltonian coordinate pencil to close all base-preserving dual automorphisms
lessons.when: The standard graph is reparameterized by arbitrary dual automorphisms over K[x,y], or only an automorphic x=0 trace is available.
lessons.use: Prove the potential trace is a coordinate over K(y) using the actual trace inverse. Keep its nonlinear square at y=0. Exhaust planes including the whole tangent plane. For a moving-y plane, extract D_a^n from the top parameter coefficient of (D_b+t*D_a)^n; the derivations need not commute. Rentschler plus the constant-Jacobian mate makes the endpoint invertible.

lessons.boundary: The written proof closes all base-preserving dual automorphisms and arbitrary R, including y-dependent and Nagata traces. It imports Rentschler through a retained primary research statement and HCTANG2 for the structural alternative. This removes one source and target coordinate without field extensions. Infinite characteristic-zero fields also give a uniform finite translation grid.

Do not apply monogenicity or translation arguments blindly over small finite fields.

Positive-characteristic universality is proved for p>N, with q>4N-13 sufficient for finite fields. Stable-class obstruction concerns 3D slices or marked data, not the unmarked fixed promoted map.
